title: Contributing to snic
text: Thanks helping improve snic! guide summarizes internal API conventions can add features confidence, especially around backends, seed helpers, message system. Please prefer focused PRs add brief rationale commit messages. Run R CMD check (devtools::check()) locally opening PR. Keep changes consistent existing style file layout. Naming Conventions Functions objects use snake_case; S3 methods follow generic.class. Examples: R/internal-utils.R:12, R/internal-grid.R:19. Examples: R/api-snic.R:1, R/api-plot.R:1. Examples: R/backend-generics.R:1, R/backend-array.R:1, R/backend-terra.R:1. Example keys: R/msg-en.R:6. Backends Live Backends adapt external image types minimal interface SNIC needs. generics defined R/backend-generics.R documented ?snic_backends. Required S3 methods implement class Cls (pick make sense data type): .check_x.Cls(x, param_name = "x") - validate input type; return x invisibly stop() friendly message. See R/backend-array.R:2 R/backend-terra.R:2. .has_crs.Cls(x) - return TRUE object carries spatial reference. See R/backend-terra.R:12. .wgs84_to_xy.Cls(x, seeds_wgs84) .xy_to_wgs84.Cls(x, seeds_xy) CRS-aware. .xy_to_rc.Cls(x, seeds_xy) .rc_to_xy.Cls(x, seeds_rc) must round-trip pixel indices map coordinates. See R/backend-terra.R:24 R/backend-terra.R:36. .x_to_arr.Cls(x) must return numeric array (height, width, bands) column-major order. See R/backend-terra.R:48. .arr_to_x.Cls(x, arr, names = NULL) must wrap single-band (h, w) array back native type, preserving extent/CRS/metadata. See R/backend-terra.R:57. .x_bbox.Cls(x) - return c(xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) object’s CRS. See R/backend-terra.R:74. Placement scaffolding: Create new file R/backend-yourpkg.R implement S3 methods class (e.g., RasterBrick, stars, magick-image). Add roxygen tags @rdname snic_backends @export method documentation NAMESPACE entries generated together generics. See patterns R/backend-array.R:1 R/backend-terra.R:1. Prefer reusing existing message keys R/msg-en.R via .msg() validation errors. Add new keys needed (see “Message helpers”). Keep conversions consistent: lat/lon  <->  (x,y)  <->  (r,c)  <->  arr. See round-trip helpers R/backend-generics.R:95. Minimal example skeleton spatial backend (pseudo-code): Tips: non-spatial data (plain arrays), ’s acceptable .wgs84_to_xy.* .xy_to_wgs84.* stop(.msg("array_no_projection_support")), R/backend-array.R:17 R/backend-array.R:23. .x_to_arr.* must normalize reorder bands - just expose raw numeric values. .arr_to_x.* validate spatial dimensions preserve metadata (names, CRS, extent) possible. Seed Helpers Use seed helpers validate, convert, build seed tables consistently. helpers return data frame standard column names depending coordinate system: Pixel indices: (r, c) Map coordinates: (x, y) Geographic coordinates (WGS84): (lat, lon) Key functions (see R/seeds.R): .seeds_check(seeds, param_name = "seeds") - validate data frame/matrix input normalize columns; returns empty (r, c) data frame NULL. See R/seeds.R:39 R/seeds.R:60. .seeds_type(seeds) - returns one "rc", "xy", "wgs84". See R/seeds.R:83. as_seeds_rc(seeds, x), as_seeds_xy(seeds, x), as_seeds_wgs84(seeds, x) - convert systems using backend methods. See R/seeds.R:22. .seeds(...) - small constructor sets names disables factors. See R/seeds.R:117. .append_seed(seeds, new_seed) - append single row, enforcing matching coordinate type. See R/seeds.R:105. Small examples: Message Helpers User-facing strings come lightweight message catalog. Use helpers R/msg.R keep errors messages uniform translateable: .msg(key, ..., lang = getOption("lang", "en")) - render message key (optionally sprintf arguments). See R/msg.R:16. .msg_load(lang, msg_lst) - register language dictionary load time. See R/msg.R:10 R/zzz.R:12. Language dictionaries live files like R/msg-en.R define named list message templates, e.g. R/msg-en.R:6. adding new messages: Choose lower_snake_case key add R/msg-en.R. Emit messages via stop(.msg("your_new_key", args...), call. = FALSE) message(.msg("...")). Development Workflow Roxygen: run devtools::document() regenerate NAMESPACE Rd files changing roxygen tags. Style: keep base R + suggested packages already use; follow patterns nearby files rather introducing new conventions. Tests: add focused tests tests/ possible. Keep runtime short. C++ core: call native code via tiny wrappers R/internal-utils.R (e.g., .snic_core(), .set_dim()). Don’t change .Call sites ad-hoc. Questions? Open issue start draft PR ask early feedback.
code: # R/backend-stars.R #' @rdname snic_backends #' @export .check_x.stars <- function(x, param_name = "x") {   if (!inherits(x, "stars")) stop(.msg("unsupported_input_type", class(x)[1]), call. = FALSE)   x }  #' @rdname snic_backends #' @export .has_crs.stars <- function(x) {   # return TRUE when CRS is present }  #' @rdname snic_backends #' @export .wgs84_to_xy.stars <- function(x, seeds_wgs84) { /* ... */ }  #' @rdname snic_backends #' @export .xy_to_rc.stars <- function(x, seeds_xy) { /* ... */ }  #' @rdname snic_backends #' @export .rc_to_xy.stars <- function(x, seeds_rc) { /* ... */ }  #' @rdname snic_backends #' @export .x_to_arr.stars <- function(x) { /* return (h, w, bands) numeric array */ }  #' @rdname snic_backends #' @export .arr_to_x.stars <- function(x, arr, names = NULL) { /* wrap back into stars */ }  .x_bbox.stars <- function(x) { /* xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax */ } # Validate and coerce seeds <- .seeds_check(data.frame(r = c(10, 30), c = c(20, 40))) stopifnot(.seeds_type(seeds) == "rc")  # Convert to map coordinates for a SpatRaster seeds_xy <- as_seeds_xy(seeds, x)  # Create a single seed and append it new_xy <- .seeds(x = 12.5, y = 34.0) seeds_xy <- .append_seed(seeds_xy, new_xy)

title: SNIC Segmentation Pipeline - Arrays
text: snic package implements Simple Non-Iterative Clustering (SNIC) algorithm image segmentation, originally proposed Achanta Susstrunk (2017). objective tutorial present segmentation pipeline compact, reproducible manner using small example. Remote sensing workflow: work terra objects, see SNIC Segmentation Pipeline - SpatRaster vignette step--step tutorial tailored multispectral imagery.

title: SNIC Segmentation Pipeline - Arrays
text: rgb array 3-channel RGB image dimensions 900 x 1200 pixels. R arrays stored column-major order, means contiguous memory layout stores pixels column moving next column. columns channel stored, new channel begins.
code: if (!requireNamespace("jpeg", quietly = TRUE)) {   stop("Install the 'jpeg' package to run this vignette.") }  # Example RGB image shipped with the package (values in [0, 1]) img_path <- system.file("demo-jpeg/clownfish.jpeg", package = "snic",   mustWork = TRUE) rgb <- jpeg::readJPEG(img_path) dim(rgb) # rows, cols, channels #> [1]  900 1200    3 snic_plot(rgb, r = 1, g = 2, b = 3)

title: SNIC Segmentation Pipeline - Arrays
text: Achanta Susstrunk (2017) use Lab color space. convert RGB image Lab, use convertColor() function grDevices package. First reshape image matrix rows image pixels columns color channels. can use snic_plot() function display Lab image visualize transformations comparing Lab channels RGB channels follows. Lab transformation done one want use multispectral images like satellite images, three channels comprise different wavelengths red, green blue. prepared image segmented can create seeds run SNIC following pipeline described .
code: dims <- dim(rgb) dim(rgb) <- c(dims[1] * dims[2], dims[3])  lab <- convertColor(rgb, from = "sRGB", to = "Lab", scale.out = 1 / 255)  # Back to canonical dimensions dim(rgb) <- dims dim(lab) <- dims # Grayscale palette gray <- grDevices::gray.colors(256)  # Prepare figure layout par(mfrow = c(2, 3))  # Plot Lab channels snic_plot(lab, band = 1, col = gray, main = "L") snic_plot(lab, band = 2, col = gray, main = "a") snic_plot(lab, band = 3, col = gray, main = "b")  # Plot RGB channels snic_plot(rgb, band = 1, col = gray, main = "R") snic_plot(rgb, band = 2, col = gray, main = "G") snic_plot(rgb, band = 3, col = gray, main = "B")

title: SNIC Segmentation Pipeline - Arrays
text: Seeds initial cluster centers. package provides function create seeds grid: snic_grid(). function takes image, type grid, spacing seeds arguments. seeds stored data frame columns r c, representing row column indices seeds image. function supports four different types grid: “rectangular”, “diamond”, “hexagonal”, “random”. spacing parameter controls spacing seeds. random seeds, spacing parameter means expected spacing seeds. density seeds inverse spacing.
code: seeds <- snic_grid(lab, type = "rectangular", spacing = 22L)

title: SNIC Segmentation Pipeline - Arrays
text: number seeds define number segments. compactness parameter controls trade-geometric distance feature similarity. greater compactness, weight given geometric distance pixels, less feature similarity. default value 0.5. , defined compactness 0.25, means algorithm balance compactness connectivity.
code: segs <- snic(lab, seeds, compactness = 0.25)

title: SNIC Segmentation Pipeline - Arrays
text: variable segs array dimensions input image, containing segment labels pixel. can used extract features image, apply image processing operations. Now followed entire pipeline, can explore different grid types compactness values see affect segmentation.
code: # Prepare figure layout par(mfrow = c(1, 1))  snic_plot(rgb, r = 1, g = 2, b = 3, seg = segs) dim(segs) #> NULL

what: Comparative grid types and compactness values
title: SNIC Segmentation Pipeline - Arrays
text: consider four seed arrangements generated snic_grid(): rectangular, diamond, hexagonal, random. built expected spacing. expect density seeds among different grid types similar given spacing. may differ slightly due geometrical boundary effects. comparison, use two compactness values: 0.1 0.5. panels display RGB image superpixel boundaries overlaid grid type (rows) compactness value (columns). moderate high compactness condition, rectangular diamond arrangements yield axis-aligned boundary structure, hexagonal randomized seeds distribute initial cluster centers evenly directions. choice among layouts task-dependent; pipeline remains : define seeds, run snic(), examine resulting segments.
code: seeds_rect <- snic_grid(rgb, type = "rectangular", spacing = 22L) seeds_diam <- snic_grid(rgb, type = "diamond", spacing = 22L) seeds_hex  <- snic_grid(rgb, type = "hexagonal", spacing = 22L)  # Set seed for reproducibility set.seed(42) seeds_rand <- snic_grid(rgb, type = "random", spacing = 22L) grids <- list(   seeds_rect, seeds_diam, seeds_hex, seeds_rand )  results <- lapply(grids, function(seeds) {   list(     snic(rgb, seeds, compactness = 0.1),     snic(rgb, seeds, compactness = 0.5)   ) }) # Prepare figure layout par(mfrow = c(4, 2), oma = c(2, 2, 2, 0))  # Plot results for (res in results) {   snic_plot(       rgb, r = 1, g = 2, b = 3, seg = res[[1]], mar = c(1, 0, 0, 0)   )   snic_plot(       rgb, r = 1, g = 2, b = 3, seg = res[[2]], mar = c(1, 0, 0, 0)   ) }  # Add column labels (compactness) mtext(   "Compactness = 0.1", side = 3,   outer = TRUE, at = 0.25,   line = 0.5, font = 1 ) mtext(   "Compactness = 0.5", side = 3,   outer = TRUE, at = 0.75,   line = 0.5, font = 1 )  # Add row labels (grid types) mtext(   "Rectangular", side = 2,   outer = TRUE, at = 3.5 / 4,   line = 0.5, font = 1, las = 3 ) mtext(   "Diamond", side = 2,   outer = TRUE, at = 2.5 / 4,   line = 0.5, font = 1, las = 3 ) mtext(   "Hexagonal", side = 2,   outer = TRUE, at = 1.5 / 4,   line = 0.5, font = 1, las = 3 ) mtext(   "Random", side = 2,   outer = TRUE, at = 0.5 / 4,   line = 0.5, font = 1, las = 3 )

title: SNIC Segmentation Pipeline - SpatRaster
text: vignette revisits SNIC segmentation pipeline, originally proposed Achanta Susstrunk (2017). works terra::SpatRaster objects, instead small -memory RGB array. use Sentinel-2 subset (demo-geotiff) ships package. Every step reflects typical remote-sensing workflow: load raster bands, seed image, run snic(), visualize resulting segments. Array workflow: prefer start -memory arrays, see SNIC Segmentation Pipeline - Arrays vignette compact tutorial mirrors tutorial without geospatial dependencies.

title: SNIC Segmentation Pipeline - SpatRaster
text: four bands cover blue (B02), red (B04), near-infrared (B08), short-wave infrared (B12) portions spectrum. snic package comes helper function plot false-color composites easily. snic_plot() understands arrays SpatRaster inputs.
code: library(terra)  data_dir <- system.file("demo-geotiff", package = "snic", mustWork = TRUE) band_files <- file.path(   data_dir,   c(     "S2_20LMR_B02_20220630.tif",     "S2_20LMR_B04_20220630.tif",     "S2_20LMR_B08_20220630.tif",     "S2_20LMR_B12_20220630.tif"   ) )  s2 <- terra::rast(band_files)  names(s2) <- c("B02", "B04", "B08", "B12") s2 #> class       : SpatRaster  #> size        : 768, 1024, 4  (nrow, ncol, nlyr) #> resolution  : 20, 20  (x, y) #> extent      : 429960, 450440, 9046000, 9061360  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) #> coord. ref. : WGS 84 / UTM zone 20S (EPSG:32720)  #> sources     : S2_20LMR_B02_20220630.tif   #>               S2_20LMR_B04_20220630.tif   #>               S2_20LMR_B08_20220630.tif   #>               S2_20LMR_B12_20220630.tif   #> names       : B02, B04, B08, B12 snic_plot(s2, r = "B08", g = "B04", b = "B02")

title: SNIC Segmentation Pipeline - SpatRaster
text: SpatRaster input, snic_grid() returns data frame latitude/longitude columns can inspected stored reproducibility. spacing padding parameters control spacing (pixels) seeds padding (pixels) around image, respectively.

title: SNIC Segmentation Pipeline - SpatRaster
text: number seeds controls number output segments. Seeds outside image ignored. compactness parameter balances spatial proximity spectral similarity; moderately low values emphasize spectral contrast, useful multispectral imagery distinct land-cover types. use compactness 0.3. result snic object contains SpatRaster spatial extent input one layer integer labels. also contains data frame per-segment feature means centroids. SpatRaster can obtained calling snic_get_seg(). labels 1-based correspond seeds order provided.
code: seg_rect <- snic(s2, seeds_rect, compactness = 0.3) seg_rect #> SNIC segmentation #>   Size (rows x cols):  768 x 1024 #> Viewing first rows and columns: #> class       : SpatRaster  #> size        : 6, 6, 1  (nrow, ncol, nlyr) #> resolution  : 20, 20  (x, y) #> extent      : 429960, 430080, 9061240, 9061360  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) #> coord. ref. : WGS 84 / UTM zone 20S (EPSG:32720)  #> source(s)   : memory #> name        : snic  #> min value   :    1  #> max value   :    1

title: SNIC Segmentation Pipeline - SpatRaster
text: plot seed locations resulting segments top false-color composite. segmentation result single-band SpatRaster whose values correspond integer labels. can extract statistics per segment convert polygons via terra::.polygons().
code: snic_plot(   s2,   r = "B08", g = "B04", b = "B02",   stretch = "lin",   seeds = seeds_rect,   seeds_plot_args = list(pch = 3, col = "#00FFFF", cex = 0.6),   seg = seg_rect,   seg_plot_args = list(border = "#FFD700", col = NA, lwd = 0.5) )

what: Comparative grid types and compactness values
title: SNIC Segmentation Pipeline - SpatRaster
text: grid types available snic_grid() operate SpatRaster objects well. Using Sentinel-2 subset, compare rectangular, diamond, hexagonal, random seeds combined two compactness settings. Rectangular diamond layouts align segments cardinal directions, whereas hexagonal random seeds spread centers evenly directions. Higher compactness induces smoother, rounded superpixels, right column contains fewer jagged boundaries left one. Regardless seed geometry, workflow stays : read multi-band raster, place seeds geographic space, call snic() desired compactness.
code: seeds_rect <- snic_grid(s2, type = "rectangular", spacing = 26) seeds_diam <- snic_grid(s2, type = "diamond", spacing = 26) seeds_hex  <- snic_grid(s2, type = "hexagonal", spacing = 26)  set.seed(42) seeds_rand <- snic_grid(s2, type = "random", spacing = 26)  grids <- list(   seeds_rect, seeds_diam,   seeds_hex, seeds_rand )  results <- lapply(grids, function(seeds) {   list(     snic(s2, seeds, compactness = 0.1),     snic(s2, seeds, compactness = 0.4)   ) }) par(mfrow = c(4, 2), oma = c(2, 2, 2, 0))  for (res in results) {   snic_plot(     s2,     r = "B08", g = "B04", b = "B02",     seg = res[[1]],     seg_plot_args = list(border = "#FFFFFF", col = NA, lwd = 0.4),     mar = c(1, 0, 0, 0)   )   snic_plot(     s2,     r = "B08", g = "B04", b = "B02",     stretch = "lin",     seg = res[[2]],     seg_plot_args = list(border = "#FFFFFF", col = NA, lwd = 0.4),     mar = c(1, 0, 0, 0)   ) }  mtext("Compactness = 0.1", side = 3, outer = TRUE, at = 0.25, line = 0.5) mtext("Compactness = 0.4", side = 3, outer = TRUE, at = 0.75, line = 0.5) mtext("Rectangular", side = 2, outer = TRUE, at = 3.5 / 4, line = 0.5, las = 3) mtext("Diamond",    side = 2, outer = TRUE, at = 2.5 / 4, line = 0.5, las = 3) mtext("Hexagonal",  side = 2, outer = TRUE, at = 1.5 / 4, line = 0.5, las = 3) mtext("Random",     side = 2, outer = TRUE, at = 0.5 / 4, line = 0.5, las = 3)

title: SNIC Segmentation Pipeline - SpatRaster
text: Spatial datasets often come multiple resolutions—example, might start 10 m grid also work 20 m 40 m aggregates faster experimentation. snic_grid() returns seeds geographic coordinates, seed set can re-used across rasters share extent CRS. generate hexagonal grid , aggregate Sentinel-2 raster four different resolutions terra::aggregate() run snic() version without touching seeds. figure compares resulting segments.
code: seeds_hex <- snic_grid(   s2,   type = "hexagonal",   spacing = 50,   padding = 5 ) par(mfrow = c(2, 2), oma = c(0, 0, 2, 0))  agg_facts <- c(1L, 2L, 4L, 8L) for (fact in agg_facts) {   s2_agg <- terra::aggregate(s2, fact = fact, fun = "mean", na.rm = TRUE)   seg_agg <- snic(s2_agg, seeds_hex, compactness = 0.2)   snic_plot(     s2_agg,     r = "B08", g = "B04", b = "B02",     seg = seg_agg,     seg_plot_args = list(border = "white", col = NA, lwd = 0.4),     main = sprintf("resolution %d m", fact * 20)   ) }

title: Superpixel Segmentation with the SNIC Algorithm
text: Seed placement controls number, shape, location resulting superpixels. package ships several grid generators, returning two-column (r, c) matrix ready snic(): snic_grid(type = "rectangular") - equally spaced seeds along rows columns. snic_grid(type = "diamond") - staggered rows produce diagonal pattern better respects gradients. snic_grid(type = "hexagonal") - hexagonal tiling isotropic superpixels. snic_grid(type = "random") - jittered seeds structure irregular prior knowledge limited. Use snic_count_seeds() forecast many superpixels spacing produce running algorithm. Seed placement strategies Sentinel-2 example (spacing = 30).
code: set.seed(42)  grid_types <- c("rectangular", "diamond", "hexagonal", "random") seed_examples <- lapply(grid_types, function(tp) {     snic_grid(s2, type = tp, spacing = 30L, padding = 0L)   } )  op <- par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(1.5, 1.5, 2, 1))  for (i in seq_along(seed_examples)) {   snic_plot(     s2,     r = 4, g = 3, b = 1,     stretch = "lin",     seeds = seed_examples[[i]],     seeds_plot_args = list(pch = 3, col = "#F6D55C", lwd = 2)   )   title(grid_types[i]) } snic_count_seeds(s2, spacing = 30L) #> [1] 850  par(op)

title: Simple Non-Iterative Clustering (SNIC) segmentation — snic
code: # Example 1: Geospatial raster if (requireNamespace("terra", quietly = TRUE)) {     path <- system.file("demo-geotiff", package = "snic", mustWork = TRUE)     files <- file.path(         path,         c(             "S2_20LMR_B02_20220630.tif",             "S2_20LMR_B04_20220630.tif",             "S2_20LMR_B08_20220630.tif",             "S2_20LMR_B12_20220630.tif"         )     )      # Downsample for speed (optional)     s2 <- terra::aggregate(terra::rast(files), fact = 8)      # Generate a regular grid of seeds (lat/lon because CRS is present)     seeds <- snic_grid(         s2,         type    = "rectangular",         spacing = 10L,         padding = 18L     )      # Run segmentation     seg <- snic(s2, seeds, compactness = 0.25)      # Visualize RGB composite with seeds and segment boundaries     snic_plot(         s2,         r = 4, g = 3, b = 1,         stretch = "lin",         seeds = seeds,         seg = seg     ) }   # Example 2: In-memory image (JPEG) + Lab transform # Uses an example image shipped with the package (no terra needed) if (requireNamespace("jpeg", quietly = TRUE)) {     img_path <- system.file(         "demo-jpeg/clownfish.jpeg",         package = "snic",         mustWork = TRUE     )     rgb <- jpeg::readJPEG(img_path) # h x w x 3 in [0, 1]      # Convert sRGB -> CIE Lab for perceptual clustering     dims <- dim(rgb)     dim(rgb) <- c(dims[1] * dims[2], dims[3])     lab <- grDevices::convertColor(         rgb,         from = "sRGB",         to = "Lab",         scale.in = 1,         scale.out = 1 / 255     )     dim(lab) <- dims     dim(rgb) <- dims      # Seeds in pixel coordinates for array inputs     seeds_rc <- snic_grid(lab, type = "hexagonal", spacing = 20L)      # Segment in Lab space and plot L channel with boundaries     seg <- snic(lab, seeds_rc, compactness = 0.1)      snic_plot(         rgb,         r = 1L,         g = 2L,         b = 3L,         seg = seg,         seg_plot_args = list(             border = "black"         )     ) }

code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Example 1: Geospatial raster if (requireNamespace("terra", quietly = TRUE)) {     # Load example multi-band image (Sentinel-2 subset) and downsample     tiff_dir <- system.file("demo-geotiff",         package = "snic",         mustWork = TRUE     )     files <- file.path(tiff_dir, c(         "S2_20LMR_B02_20220630.tif",         "S2_20LMR_B04_20220630.tif",         "S2_20LMR_B08_20220630.tif",         "S2_20LMR_B12_20220630.tif"     ))     s2 <- terra::aggregate(terra::rast(files), fact = 8)      # Compare grid types visually using snic_plot for immediate feedback     types <- c("rectangular", "diamond", "hexagonal", "random")     par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(2, 2, 2, 2))     for (tp in types) {         seeds <- snic_grid(s2, type = tp, spacing = 12L, padding = 18L)         snic_plot(             s2,             r = 4, g = 3, b = 1, stretch = "lin",             seeds = seeds,             main = paste("Grid:", tp)         )     }     par(mfrow = c(1, 1))      # Estimate seed counts for planning     snic_count_seeds(s2, spacing = 12L, padding = 18L) }  # Example 2: In-memory image (JPEG) if (requireNamespace("jpeg", quietly = TRUE)) {     img_path <- system.file(         "demo-jpeg/clownfish.jpeg",         package = "snic",         mustWork = TRUE     )     rgb <- jpeg::readJPEG(img_path)      # Compare grid types visually using snic_plot for immediate feedback     types <- c("rectangular", "diamond", "hexagonal", "random")     par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(2, 2, 2, 2))     for (tp in types) {         seeds <- snic_grid(rgb, type = tp, spacing = 12L, padding = 18L)         snic_plot(             rgb,             r = 1, g = 2, b = 3,             seeds = seeds,             main = paste("Grid:", tp)         )     }     par(mfrow = c(1, 1)) } } # }

Ignored RGB plots. stretch Character string indicating contrast-stretching method. Determines band values scaled \([0, 1]\) range plotting. One : "lin": linear stretch based minimum maximum     values (default). "hist": histogram equalization (redistribute values     equalize color histogram).
